variants.title: Name the record
variants.context: Three records have different jobs: the payment intent tracks what the customer and merchant are trying to do; the provider attempt tracks one request to an external processor and its uncertain outcome; the ledger journal records money owed or moved and must balance to zero. An ambiguous result becomes processing, never a guess.
variants.prompt: A provider call times out. Which record captures that uncertain outcome?
optionFeedback: The attempt tracks one request and its uncertain result.
The intent tracks what the parties are trying to do.
The journal records completed monetary effect.
variants.hint: Which record is per external request?
variants.explanation: Timeouts, duplicates, and late webhooks are normal.

variants.prompt: Which statement about the ledger is correct?
options: Every journal balances to zero within one currency and is append-only.
Journals may be edited to fix mistakes.
The provider webhook is the financial truth.
optionFeedback: Webhooks are evidence, not the sole source of truth.
variants.hint: What does a balanced journal guarantee?
variants.explanation: Neither a cache nor a webhook is the sole source of financial truth.

variants.prompt: The API returned success but the provider outcome is unknown. What state should the payment be in?
options: processing, with durable ownership of an unresolved outcome and recovery scheduled.
optionFeedback: Ambiguity becomes processing, never a guess.
variants.hint: Which states are final only with evidence?
variants.explanation: succeeded and failed are final only with evidence.

variants.title: Use the terms precisely
variants.context: Authorize reserves spending capacity and may expire. Capture requests completion and creates the ledger obligation. Settle exchanges funds later and can disagree temporarily. Refund is a new reversal operation; it cannot exceed captured minus earlier refunds.
variants.prompt: An authorization succeeded but the merchant has not captured. Has money moved?
options: No. Authorization reserves capacity; capture creates the obligation; settlement moves funds later.
variants.hint: Which step creates the ledger obligation?
variants.explanation: Capture creates the merchant-facing financial obligation.

variants.title: Use the terms precisely
variants.context: Authorize reserves spending capacity and may expire. Capture requests completion and creates the ledger obligation. Settle exchanges funds later and can disagree temporarily. Refund is a new reversal operation; it cannot exceed captured minus earlier refunds.
variants.prompt: A $100 capture has a $30 refund. A second refund request is for $80. What happens?
options: Rejected: a refund cannot exceed captured minus earlier refunds, which is $70.
optionFeedback: Splitting does not raise the cap.
variants.hint: How much has already been refunded?
variants.explanation: A refund is a new reversal operation against captured value.

variants.prompt: Settlement reports disagree with yesterday’s capture status. What is the right response?
options: Reconcile: compare attempts and journals with provider transactions and investigate differences.
optionFeedback: Reconciliation is the designed response to disagreement.
Ledgers are append-only; corrections are new journals.

variants.title: Estimate the load
variants.context: Baseline: 100 million attempts per day, 10× peak, about 12K provider calls per second at peak, 800 ms average provider latency, four asynchronous event deliveries per attempt.
variants.prompt: 100 million attempts per day with a 10× peak. What is the peak attempts per second, rounded to the nearest whole number?

mistakes.feedback: Multiply by ten, not one hundred.

variants.title: Estimate the load
variants.context: Baseline: 100 million attempts per day, 10× peak, about 12K provider calls per second at peak, 800 ms average provider latency, four asynchronous event deliveries per attempt.
variants.prompt: 12,000 provider calls per second with 800 ms average provider latency. How many calls are in flight, by Little’s Law?
variants.explanation: 12,000 × 0.8 = 9,600 concurrent calls before headroom; size connection pools accordingly.

mistakes.feedback: Multiply by 0.8 seconds, do not divide.

variants.title: Estimate the load
variants.context: Baseline: 100 million attempts per day, 10× peak, about 12K provider calls per second at peak, 800 ms average provider latency, four asynchronous event deliveries per attempt.
variants.prompt: Consumers fall 20,000 events per second behind for five minutes. How many deliveries accumulate?
variants.explanation: 20,000 × 300 = 6,000,000 deliveries; recovery capacity must exceed live arrivals or the queue never drains.

variants.title: Make the charge singular
variants.context: One merchant-scoped idempotency key maps to one request fingerprint and one result. Same key with different parameters is a conflict. Provider retries amplify external calls but do not increase legitimate intents.
variants.prompt: A merchant retries a create-payment call with the same idempotency key but a different amount. What happens?
options: Conflict: the key maps to one request fingerprint and one result.
optionFeedback: A different fingerprint under the same key is rejected.
Duplicates are the failure this prevents.
variants.hint: What is bound to the key?
variants.explanation: One key, one fingerprint, one result.

variants.title: Make the charge singular
variants.context: One merchant-scoped idempotency key maps to one request fingerprint and one result. Same key with different parameters is a conflict. Provider retries amplify external calls but do not increase legitimate intents.
variants.prompt: Provider retries doubled during an outage while intent creation was flat. What should the dashboard show?
options: Both rates separately: request throughput can hide duplicate-charge risk.
optionFeedback: Retries amplify external calls without adding intents.
variants.hint: Which number changed, and which did not?
variants.explanation: Track provider calls and legitimate intents separately.

variants.prompt: Two webhook events for the same attempt arrive out of order: succeeded, then a late processing. What should the handler do?
options: Ignore the late processing event; transitions are monotonic.
Move the payment back to processing.
variants.explanation: Stable provider references and monotonic handlers turn duplicates into bounded work.

variants.title: Own compliance deliberately
variants.context: Use provider-hosted fields or tokenization so application servers never receive card numbers. Keep card security codes out of logs and storage. Architecture can reduce compliance scope; it cannot declare the organization compliant.
variants.prompt: Application servers receive raw card numbers from the checkout form. What changes the picture?
options: Provider-hosted fields or tokenization so servers never see the primary account number.
optionFeedback: Keep the PAN out of application services.
Logs should never contain it in the first place.
variants.hint: Which component should touch the card number?

variants.title: Own compliance deliberately
variants.context: Use provider-hosted fields or tokenization so application servers never receive card numbers. Keep card security codes out of logs and storage. Architecture can reduce compliance scope; it cannot declare the organization compliant.
variants.prompt: A debug log line includes the card security code. What is the rule?
options: Card security codes must never be logged or stored.
Delete the log after a day.
optionFeedback: Keep CVC out of logs and storage entirely.
Retention does not fix prohibited storage.
variants.explanation: Apply retention to customer data without deleting required financial records.

variants.title: Own compliance deliberately

variants.prompt: Does a well-designed architecture make the organization PCI compliant?
options: No. It reduces scope; compliance is a legal and security workstream with named owners.
optionFeedback: Document who owns authentication, fraud, disputes, onboarding, and reporting.
Tokenization reduces scope; it does not declare compliance.
variants.explanation: Treat PCI DSS, privacy, sanctions, and AML as workstreams.
